doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

chapter: Staying in Rome and best and worst gigs
title: Dolores Mancuso and Sal Amico's sense of time
summary: Singers and horn players with their own time make accompanying easier. Sal Amico would warm up like an engine and then take off.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I know you’ve mentioned one thing that I think you very much like is when a horn player or a singer has their own sense of time. You used to tell me to listen to Dolores [Mancuso] how she, and Sal Amico too.

Right. Yes. Yeah. Those are people, you don’t have to make the box for. They’re in the box by themselves. We are all sharing the same concept. So you can do what you have to. You don’t have to feel obligated to square everything off and set a foundation for them. So it makes it more interesting and more fun to play that way. You can stretch out behind them. Sal, once he started playing he didn’t need anything.
Once he started playing. I remember I used to watch him and he’d just be going [soft scatting], and then all of a sudden like, oh, when did the song start?
Yeah. He was like cranking the engine, turning it, getting all the cylinders firing and then, once they started firing bango.
